note: THE ONE VECTOR SET of the blind document's cell (media.md item 4, TWO SCHEMAS, TWO VECTOR SETS, ONE CLASSIFICATION, ONE CAP; the blind-document investigation section 5 (i); the rulings s6-D3, bd-D1, bd-D3; PATTERNS P5): the mirror of cells.json for the second kind, run by every parser of the cell -- skepd's media/blind.rs, the shell's, the browser page's -- in its own gate. The rule is the arbiter: parse(b) answers a blind cell only where b == encode(parse(b)). `verdict` is `cell` (admitted: the body IS the canonical form) or `no_cell`; `names_kind` says whether the body's `type` member names THIS kind, which is what a reader whose null permits a permanent act halts on (DOCTRINE D13's carve-out) -- the daemon's write door refuses such a value by name (unknown_cell_schema) and the fetch route answers it by the same name; a body naming the picture's kind is the picture parser's and names nothing to this one. A blind cell carries a commitment and nothing else: no size (bd-D3), no hash -- nothing the board can read a file by. The cap is the picture kind's, one for every media cell kind. Each pin here is INTERIM (the board's sm-Q8).

vectors.name: canonical
vectors.why: the one form: type, commitment in that order, no whitespace, 64 lowercase hex, nothing else

vectors.name: canonical_zero_commitment
vectors.why: a commitment is 32 bytes of the owner's choosing; the schema judges form, the owner's client judges the key

vectors.name: size_member
vectors.why: the blind cell carries no size (bd-D3): a size discloses the file's length, which the board must not learn

vectors.name: hash_member
vectors.why: a hash would let a holder of a candidate file confirm it against the board (M-I2 (i)); the commitment is keyed so it cannot

vectors.name: two_commitment_members
vectors.why: the two-commitment body: a parser could bind one and a reader check the other; refused by the canonical rule at every parser

vectors.name: member_order
vectors.why: the members in any other order round-trip to different bytes

vectors.name: uppercase_hex
vectors.why: the commitment is 64 LOWERCASE hex characters; uppercase re-encodes lowercase and fails the compare

vectors.name: hex_63
vectors.why: 63 hex characters are no 32-byte commitment

vectors.name: hex_65
vectors.why: 65 hex characters are no 32-byte commitment

vectors.name: hex_not_hex
vectors.why: a non-hex character in the commitment

vectors.name: whitespace
vectors.why: parses to the same cell and re-encodes to different bytes: b != encode(parse(b))

vectors.name: trailing_byte
vectors.why: a trailing byte: JSON admits it, the canonical rule does not

vectors.name: extent_member
vectors.why: the v1 cell carries no extent member (ms5-D2): a video-era member is a second schema

vectors.name: designation_member
vectors.why: H1: a value naming the kind under a second schema's form parses under no pinned schema; the daemon halts on it, never admits it as absent

vectors.name: empty_commitment
vectors.why: an empty string is no 32-byte commitment

vectors.name: commitment_not_a_string
vectors.why: the commitment is a string

vectors.name: missing_commitment
vectors.why: the arity is closed: two members, each present

vectors.name: picture_kind
vectors.why: a type naming the picture's kind is the picture parser's, which reads it under its own schema (and halts on it there: a commitment is no picture cell); it names nothing to this one

vectors.name: another_kind
vectors.why: a type naming another kind (the enrollment record's) is not the cell's; its own schema reads it

vectors.name: no_type
vectors.why: no type member names no kind (D13: every record body names its type)

vectors.name: prose
vectors.why: prose is no JSON object

vectors.name: not_json
vectors.why: not JSON at all (unterminated): every schema is JSON, so nothing names the kind here

vectors.name: json_array
vectors.why: a cell inside an array is no cell: the value is one object

vectors.name: round_trips_to_other_bytes
vectors.why: one space before the closing brace: the same cell under JSON, other bytes under the rule

vectors.name: past_the_cap
vectors.why: a body past the cell's cap (1024 bytes, the picture kind's and every media kind's) is parsed by no reader of a cell, but the cap bounds the parse and never the classification: it opens with the blind kind's canonical opening, so it names the kind under no schema this build reads — refused unknown_cell_schema at the door; no halt mark, the index's entry path reading the picture kind's opening alone

vectors.name: past_the_cap_not_naming
vectors.why: a body past the cap that opens with no kind's canonical opening — the kind named later in the body — is parsed by no reader of a cell and names nothing at every parser: no cell of any schema, an ordinary value
